contradictsARecordInThisRepo.itSays: 'their canonical.pdf and boundary.pdf differ only in the invisible /Title metadata string'
contradictsARecordInThisRepo.measuredInstead: False of these bytes, and the bytes have not moved: al-pardoned-felony-set and al-felony-nonconviction-90-set carry the same canonical and boundary SHA-256 at b311ef066 (the commit that note was written against) and at deead9f25. Within each family the two fixtures differ in visible field content on nine of eleven pages, and this run's own page images differ on nine of eleven. The /Title-only identity is real but it lies BETWEEN THE TWO FAMILIES, not between the two fixtures: al-pardoned-felony-set and al-felony-nonconviction-90-set deliver the same 22 page images, byte for byte, canonical and boundary alike.
contradictsARecordInThisRepo.whatStandsUnchanged: The rest of the note holds exactly. Both families produce clean RASTER_PASS receipts with zero problems; their 22 page images are byte-identical to each other; neither ticks any eligibility box on the CR-65 it files; the raster gate cannot see any of this and the importer would have admitted both.

howThisWasMeasured: Page-image identity from the three families' own RCAP_RECEIPT_INVENTORY payloads, extracted programmatically from the saved job-log responses; no digest was retyped. Checkbox state, /Info keys and per-page content streams from the delivered PDFs at deead9f25 with pikepdf and pdftotext, not from any build report.
grantsNothing: A refusal here withholds static family admission only. It sets no verdict, promotes nothing, opens no route, closes no route and asserts nothing about production. RASTER_PASS on these two families remains what the central workflow recorded.
